validity.recommendation: No existence/classification/duplicate/attribution defect found. GTN is a real, FERC-jurisdictional interstate natural-gas transmission mainline running from Kingsgate, BC (Idaho/British Columbia border) to Malin, OR, currently operated as Gas Transmission Northwest LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary of TC Pipelines, LP, which is in turn a wholly owned subsidiary of TC Energy Corporation since the March 2021 take-private merger. Confirmed operating via FERC's Oct 23, 2023 certificate order (185 FERC 61,035, Docket CP22-2-000) and TC Energy's own current operations page. Not a duplicate: the similarly-named 'Northwest Pipeline' (Williams Companies' separate Rockies/Pacific NW system) is a different pipeline entirely and is not on this 46-row roster -- a genuine near-miss name that was checked and dismissed.
validity.researcher_notes: Existence/classification confirmed via FERC docket CP22-2-000 (185 FERC 61,035, Oct 23 2023) https://aglaw.psu.edu (PSU law-school mirror of the FERC order text; original FERC eLibrary copy is unfetchable/garbled) and TC Energy's live operations page https://www.tcenergy.com/operations/natural-gas/gas-transmission-northwest/ -- both describe GTN in the present tense as an active interstate mainline under FERC's NGA jurisdiction. A worthwhile attribution note for future researchers: CPUC Decision No. 60564 (Aug 16, 1960) states 'Pacific Gas and Electric Company filed this application on January 9, 1959 ... for the construction ... of a 36-inch natural gas pipeline from the California-Oregon border to Antioch. This pipeline will form the California portion of a project...' -- that 1959 filing date is PG&E's own CALIFORNIA-INTRASTATE certificate application for the 296-mile CA-only portion, a DIFFERENT entity/scope than this row's FERC-jurisdictional interstate P.G.T./GTN mainline. Using 1959 as GTN's own ProposalYear would be a misattribution across two related-but-distinct regulatory filings; deliberately NOT used (see Proposal[ref] fill, left UNRESOLVED).

An earlier draft of this research (pre-compaction) had mistakenly synthesized ~2850 MMcf/d from a WebSearch AI summary that conflated multiple TC Energy figures; re-checking the actual underlying page text corrected this to 2700, matching FERC exactly. Filed as a REFS_ADDED fill with the corrected value (2700.00), paired with this SPEC-concern validity entry.

Per the repo's FuelSource gotcha (docs/reference/gem_schema.md), FuelSource must name an upstream field/facility, never a generic commodity term. GTN draws gas broadly from the Western Canada Sedimentary Basin (WCSB) via interconnection at Kingsgate/Station 2 (NOVA Gas Transmission Ltd / TC Energy's Alberta System) -- a very large multi-field, multi-operator basin, not one named field or plant, and judged too generic/jurisdiction-spanning to count as a valid FuelSource fill (contrast sibling shard P0158/Bison Pipeline, where 'Powder River Basin' was accepted as a valid, specifically-named single-basin FuelSource -- WCSB is a materially larger, less specific comparator and was judged not to meet the same bar). EIA's GTN XPress project notes name 'Tourmaline Oil Mktng Corp' as a contracted SHIPPER for the newest capacity increment, not an upstream field/facility -- does not qualify as a FuelSource fill either. Left UNRESOLVED.
